mode.title: what the table shows
mode.description: blend: the weighted blend (rows, columns, the sum). matrix: a schematic rating matrix and what each recommender sees of it. mnar: the same matrix, its gaps are not random. pseudo: a content-based model fills the empty cells of a sparse matrix with pseudo-ratings, the collaborative model reads it, and the weight of a pair of users grows with their real ratings. split (WP-74): a rating matrix is split into training, validation and test ratings, how the three are used, and a q-fold cross-validation. errors (WP-74): rating error: real and predicted stars, the absolute errors and MAE, the squared errors and RMSE, one bad prediction that moves RMSE more than MAE, which one to use, the long tail. confusion (WP-74): a 2 x 2 table of what a recommender did against what the user liked, in two views (`outcomes`: the four outcomes, the two errors, which is worse, accuracy, class imbalance; `measures`: precision, recall, the trade-off, F1, specificity). dcg (WP-74): a ranked list scored by gain and position: the discount, DCG, the ideal order, NDCG, the same perfect item first and late, and why the top should weigh more. timeline (WP-74): interactions on a time axis: a random split learns from the future, a temporal split does not, the Netflix idea, a taste that changes, and a winner that depends on the split. exposure (WP-74): why the missing ratings are not random: a toy rating matrix whose cells are rated, shown but not rated, or never shown; the ratings pile up high; popular films against the long tail; three remedies (a random test sample, unbiased estimators such as IPS, sensitivity analysis); four presses. catalog (WP-74): catalogue coverage of two recommenders on a toy catalogue of 20 films, then prediction coverage on a user x film grid (a new user and a new film leave gaps); four presses. pairs (WP-74): intra-list diversity: a list of three films, the similarity of each of its three pairs, diversity as the mean dissimilarity, and diversity told apart from accuracy; three presses. Every mode takes four presses except split, errors, confusion, dcg and timeline, which take five, and pairs, which takes three.

table-highlight.steps: Four presses in every mode. blend: the base recommenders' predictions for the new film (stars and numbers), their weights (bars; a negative weight leans left and is marked), the products, then the products travel into the sum, the total lands and fills the film's stars. matrix: what the collaborative, the content-based and the knowledge-based recommender each see of a rating matrix, then their three blind spots together. mnar: the observed ratings pile up high, the held-out ratings come from the same selection, the screen outside the matrix was never measured, accuracy is not the only measure. pseudo (WP-50): the real ratings of a sparse matrix, the pseudo-ratings of a content-based model fill every empty cell, the filled vectors of two users side by side with an arc of similar taste, then the weight multipliers of three pairs of users (a bar that grows with their real ratings and is full from `full` of them; the counts are shown, the bars carry no number). groups (WP-50): the three groups of inputs (ids, film content, user profile), one model that reads them all, its predicted rating, a film with only two ratings (synthetic) for which the box of the ids dims and the film content lights up, then the three arrows washed in gold together. split (WP-74, five presses): the validation and test ratings of a rating matrix are veiled (hold-out), every rating takes its role (training, validation, test; colour and shape) with the counts in a bar, the three uses as cards (a lock on the test ratings), the same as an exam (textbook, practice exams, the final), then a q-fold cross-validation (q rows, one test part each, a bar per fold and the bar of their average). errors (WP-74, five presses): six real and predicted ratings; a bar and a number for every absolute error and the MAE card; the squared errors and the RMSE card; a seventh, bad pair and how much each value grows (MAE +71 %, RMSE +145 %); what each error counts; the long tail (popular items set the average, sparse items have larger errors). confusion (WP-74; WP-93, D-177: five presses in the view outcomes, SIX in the view measures): view outcomes: the four outcomes TP, FP, FN, TN, Type I and II errors, which is worse (two opposite tasks: a film, where a bad pick is worse, and a lawyer looking for precedents, where a missed case is worse), accuracy with its gauge, and the imbalanced case where accuracy looks excellent and nothing is found; view measures: precision (the row recommended), recall (the column liked), specificity (the column not liked), the matrix of one famous band and its card (precision high, recall low), the matrix of all of rock and its card (the reverse), then F1 next to the wrong average. dcg (WP-74, five presses): the gains of a five-item list; the discount bar of every position; gain x discount and the DCG; the ideal order, IDCG and NDCG with a gauge; one perfect item first and 15th (NDCG 1.00 and 0.25); the weight of every position in ROC and Kendall (flat) and in NDCG (falling) with the cut points @10 and @20. timeline (WP-74, five presses): interactions of four users on a time axis; the random split with the test interactions that have training ones after them; the temporal split and its cut line; the newest two interactions of every user (Netflix); the first user's taste changing (a new shape); two leaderboards, one per split, that name different winners (a synthetic-data tag). exposure (WP-74, four presses): the rated cells of a matrix of 6 users x 8 films appear with a histogram of the ratings against the ratings if every film were rated (users rate what they like); the never-shown cells get a hatched veil and a legend (you cannot rate what you were never shown); the films split into popular and long tail with a count bar under each film and two error bars (a synthetic-data tag); the matrix steps back for three remedies (a random test sample, unbiased estimators such as IPS, sensitivity analysis). catalog (WP-74, four presses): a popularity recommender lights the same few films of a catalogue of 20; a varied one lights many more; catalogue coverage as a gauge and a fraction under each catalogue; prediction coverage: the user x film pairs the system can predict (a tick), the gaps of a new user and a new film, the fraction and the note that coverage is read with accuracy. pairs (WP-74, three presses): a list of three films of one genre and the similarity of each of its three pairs; a list of three genres beside it, each list with its intra-list diversity (the mean of 1 - similarity, a number and a gauge); two pills (accuracy a little lower, satisfaction higher) and the gold sentence that diversity can be told apart from accuracy.

mode.title: what the pipeline shows
mode.description: cascade: films pass a rough first recommender and a second one that only settles ties (six presses). switch: a switch at the entrance and two ways, chosen by how many ratings the user has or by a measurement (four presses). designs: the two designs of an ensemble of recommenders, parallel and sequential, as boxes and arrows ending in a combiner, and the designs of the taxonomy that belong to each (three presses). kinds: what an ensemble reads, one kind of data into three different models or two kinds of data into two models, both into a weighted blend, the weights of the second coming forward (three presses). meta: a content-based model learns a profile for each user, the collaborative model compares users by these profiles, then feature augmentation (an output is handed on) against meta-level (the model itself is) (three presses). flow (WP-74): a flow of people and data through a split and a score, in three views (ab: an A/B test, data: the Netflix Prize data split, score: a public quiz and a hidden test), four presses in each.

pipeline.steps: cascade mode, six presses: the candidates appear, the first recommender ranks them roughly (many tie), it cuts the weakest, the ties are bracketed and the second recommender scores only them, it orders each tie inside its group, then the verdict (same groups, the single item stayed put, cut items do not return). switch mode, four presses: a new user (three ratings) is switched to the content-based way, a user with a long history to the collaborative way, the bucket of models picks the winner by held-out error, then wrong (by training error) next to right (by held-out error). designs mode, three presses: the parallel design (an input, two recommenders side by side, a combiner, a prediction), the sequential design (a chain that ends in the same combiner, with two dashed arrows that may also be there: the original input to the next recommender and the earlier output to the combiner), then two chips under each panel naming the designs of the taxonomy that belong to it, in the order of the tree. kinds mode, three presses: the homogeneous panel (one box of data, three different models, a weighted blend, a prediction), the heterogeneous panel (two boxes of data of two kinds, a collaborative and a content-based model, the same blend; the upper panel goes quiet), then the weights of the lower panel come forward (the two arrows into the blend drawn again, thicker, with the labels w1 and w2). meta mode, three presses: the content-based model learns a profile (one card, a user and three bars), two more users and the pill that joins the two alike profiles while the collaborative model reads the three, then two rows, feature augmentation (an output, a rating, is handed on) above meta-level (the model itself is). flow (WP-74, four presses in each of three views): ab: a crowd of 24 users is split at random into two groups, each gets an algorithm for the same period, the conversion rate of each group, and the margins that overlap (one day is not enough); data: the Netflix Prize data on its time axis, the newest ratings of every user held out (qualifying), split into quiz and test with the probe inside the training data, then the shares to scale; score: a team sends a prediction file, the quiz half is scored in public, the test half is locked away and decides the prize, and tuning to the public score is crossed out.

compare.steps: lists mode, three presses: a long-history user's home page shows two lists side by side (content-based and collaborative); the newly released film appears only in the content-based list (the collaborative list has an empty place); nothing is merged, the user reads both. families mode, four presses (WP-50): bagging (three resamples of the data with replacement, each into a model, three synthetic predictions averaged), boosting (a chain of three models, the examples a model gets wrong ringed and grown for the next, a weighted vote), stacking (three base models, their predictions as columns, a second-level learner, one prediction), and the same ideas for rating matrices (resampled ratings, k of 2k neighbours, two random starts of a factorization); every picture is schematic. ranked (WP-74): view topk (five presses): a list of 20 and the window of what the user sees; the relevant items (stars, with a key) and the two cut points 10 and 20; the sixth relevant item at rank 50, outside the list, with the false negatives of each cut marked, precision and recall at the two cuts as computations and TP, FP and FN told; that item framed as not found; one hidden item per user (leave-one-out) with the hit rate HR@10 and the average reciprocal hit rank ARHR; view corr (three presses): Spearman and Kendall on five items and a tie in the true order; view sampled (four presses): Rendle's three hypothetical algorithms A, B and C on the full ranking and on 99 sampled negatives (Recall@10 and NDCG, then AP), the order of the three that flips, and the rule (a hypothetical-example tag). why (WP-74, four presses): a shopper's weekly basket (banana, bread, milk, eggs); list A is the basket again, every item a hit and none of them new; list B is one product the shopper has never tried (cheese): it may miss, a hit really helps; the two questions come apart (where do we test: a live system or a lab; what do we measure: prediction success or benefit); the gold sentence: a right prediction is not a good recommendation. novelty (WP-74, six presses since WP-93): a user who loves one director's films gets three cards with their yes/no attributes (new to the user, unexpected, the user likes it): a film the user has watched (known), the director's new film (new, but expected) and a film of another genre the user would never search for (serendipity, a double gold frame); then the nested sets (every serendipity is new), the two ways of measuring (online: did you know it, did you like it; offline: expected means what a primitive recommender suggests) and the gold sentence; 5 novelty as surprise (Zhou et al. 2010): the cards leave and the three films return as rows with k, log2(u / k), a bar of I in bits and its value, the mean of the list under them (toy numbers: u = 1,024 users, k = 512, 128 and 8 give 1, 3 and 7 bits, mean 3.67); 6 serendipity as a share (Ge et al. 2010): ten films, the primitive recommender's films dimmed and tagged PM, a frame round the unexpected ones (RS minus PM), a tick or a cross under them, unexpected = 10 - 6 = 4 and S = 3 / 4 = 0.75. columns (WP-74, four presses): two or three columns (a title, a picture, ticked, crossed, plain or boxed formula lines; density tight for five short lines each) come in press by press, a line may rise into a column that is already there, and up to three footer lines (a number, a gold sentence) close the story; examples: user study, online and offline; confidence and trust, robustness and scalability; the offline table and online.

figureLabel.en: A chart of published test RMSE values of the Netflix Prize, lower is better, with the milestones in order. Cinematch scored 0.9525 on the test set (0.9514 on the quiz set). The 2007 Progress Prize reached 0.8723 and the 2008 Progress Prize 0.8627. The Grand Prize ended in a tie at 0.8567 on 26 July 2009 between BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos (18:18:28) and The Ensemble (18:38:22); the earlier submission won. The target was 0.8572, 10% better than Cinematch. Beside the chart, a card of three numbers Netflix gave for what ran in production: SVD 0.8914, RBM 0.8990 and their linear blend 0.88, with the set not stated.
figureLabel.tr: Netflix Ödülü'nün yayımlanmış test RMSE değerlerinin grafiği; düşük olan iyidir, kilometre taşları sırayla. Cinematch test kümesinde 0,9525 aldı (quiz kümesinde 0,9514). 2007 İlerleme Ödülü 0,8723'e, 2008 İlerleme Ödülü 0,8627'ye ulaştı. Büyük Ödül, 26 Temmuz 2009'da BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos (18:18:28) ile The Ensemble (18:38:22) arasında 0,8567'de beraberlikle bitti; önce gönderilen kazandı. Hedef, Cinematch'ten %10 iyi olan 0,8572'ydi. Grafiğin yanında Netflix'in üretimde çalışan şey için verdiği üç sayının kartı: SVD 0,8914, RBM 0,8990 ve doğrusal karışımları 0,88; hangi kümede ölçüldükleri belirtilmemiş.

chart-draw.steps: Mode milestones, four presses: 1 the published test RMSE of Cinematch with its line, the target line (10 per cent better) and the bracket between them; 2 the progress prizes of 2007 and 2008 and the Grand Prize come one after the other on a ladder of milestones (not a time axis), the Grand Prize is a tie of two teams at the same height with their submission times, the earlier submission won; 3 the leaderboard dims and a card of its own shows what ran in production (three numbers, set not stated); 4 both are washed in gold together. Mode vote, seven presses (six without the worse curve): 1 the village fair of Galton (the dressed weight of an ox and the middle of 787 guesses on a number line); 2 the chance that the majority is right for independent members, each right 75 % of the time, at n = 1 and 5; 3 the rest of the curve (n = 9 and 17 written); 4 copies of one model: a flat dashed line, no gain; 5 members that are right only 40 % of the time: the vote gets worse (optional, empty `worse.points` drops it); 6 the chart dims for a bar of squared bias + variance + noise in invented proportions (tagged synthetic data); 7 the chart returns and the gap between the independent curve and the flat line is washed in gold. Mode finish (WP-74), five presses, the whole ladder on the test set: 1 the movie average (1.0540); 2 Cinematch (0.9525, its quiz value 0.9514 beside it) and a line down to it; 3 the dashed target line (0.8572, 10 per cent better) and the 2007 and 2008 progress prizes (0.8723, 0.8627); 4 the two finalists at the same height (test 0.8567, a tie at four decimals, the winner a filled point and the runner-up a ring) and a card: on the public quiz the order was the reverse (0.8553 and 0.8554); 5 six decimals (0.856704 and 0.856714), the earlier submission wins (19 min 54 s earlier) and the leaderboard did not decide the winner. Mode roc (WP-74, five presses since WP-93): 1 one ranked list of ten with five relevant items, unnamed, and a cut that slides down it (the top k is recommended): the four counts TP, FP, FN, TN and the open formulas TPR = TP / (TP + FN) and FPR = FP / (FP + TN) show the numbers of every k, a point drops onto the chart at (FPR, TPR) and the ROC curve builds behind it step by step (a relevant item up, an irrelevant one right), the cut walks the first `first` ranks (default 4); 2 the cut runs on to the end of the list, faster, and the curve is complete at (1, 1); 3 the walk machinery leaves, the oracle (every relevant item first) is the best curve and a random list is the diagonal, on average; 4 the first list is named algorithm A and a second list, B, is walked: A is ahead at the start and B later, the curves cross; 5 the area under the curve of B is shaded: AUC = the pairs with the relevant item first over all pairs (A 15 / 25 = 0.60, B 16 / 25 = 0.64) and AUC is blind to position. Mode seeds (WP-74), four presses: 1 a single split: the spread over eight seeds inside the measured band of 6.3 % (synthetic dots); 2 cross-validation: the band of 2.3 %; 3 an untuned baseline as reported (RMSE 0.8197) against the same baseline run carefully (0.7633) and the best reported method (0.7634); 4 5 of 26 papers repeated the seeds, more than half of the new-algorithm papers have no significance test, and the gold sentence: one run is an anecdote.
